question: Do Hebrew structural trajectories that appear unresolved at an inherited verse boundary continue into the actual adjacent verse in a way that is more coherent with within-verse first-passage structure than a matched shuffled next-verse splice?
claimBoundary: A positive result supports the claim that at least some inherited verse divisions cut across the structural process measured by this anonymous four-history first-passage projector. It does not show that verse divisions are meaningless, that every process crosses them, that chapter boundaries are process boundaries, or that Hebrew and glyphs share a grammar. Failure would reject only this boundary-continuity test under the frozen projector and control construction.

split.reason: All adjacent verses used by a boundary-continuity comparison must remain in the same custody lane; the older verse-hash split is therefore not reused for V25 modeling.
split.hardBoundary: chapter end; V25 does not cross chapter boundaries

projector.state: anonymous equality pattern of previous four identities in the same representation, padded by <START>
projector.origin: an operator occurrence inside a non-final verse whose V24-style first passage does not leave its immediate post-operator state S1 before the inherited verse boundary
projector.realContinuation: append the actual immediately adjacent verse in the same chapter and scan only that next verse for the first anonymous state F different from S1
projector.shuffledContinuation: append a deterministic matched next-verse splice from another eligible boundary in the same custody lane, preferably same book and lemma-token-count bin, never the actual next verse; scan exactly one shuffled verse for first F different from S1
projector.resolvedTrainingEvent: an occurrence whose first anonymous state F different from S1 is observed before the end of its own verse; these events alone train the within-verse destination model
projector.distance: number of subsequent operators from the origin to F; descriptive only and never used for eligibility, model selection, or adjudication

shuffleControl.primaryGrouping: custody lane + book + target-next-verse lemma-token-count bin
shuffleControl.fallbackGrouping: custody lane + book when a primary group has fewer than two boundaries
shuffleControl.finalFallback: custody lane when a book group has fewer than two boundaries
shuffleControl.assignment: sort origin boundaries by sha256(salt + anonymous origin verse id), then cyclically rotate target next-verse ids by one; groups of size one after final fallback are excluded

training.outcomeAlphabet: all 24 canonical four-history anonymous states generated structurally; no unit-end category

withinVerseDestinationModel.additive: Padd(F|S0,S1,o) proportional to Pcontext * Poperator / Pbase, then renormalized
withinVerseDestinationModel.trainingData: TRAIN resolved-within-verse events only; boundary-hit events never train this destination model
withinVerseDestinationModel.purpose: measure whether a post-boundary destination looks like the same structural process observed when trajectories resolve inside verses

evaluation.primaryContrast: For origins where both real and shuffled adjacent verses yield a departure F, compute log2 Padd(F_real|S0,S1,o) - log2 Padd(F_shuffle|S0,S1,o), average within operator, then equally across operators.
evaluation.pairedNull: independently sign-flip each evaluable operator's real-minus-shuffled mean coherence difference; exact enumeration when <=12 operators, otherwise 4096 deterministic sign flips
evaluation.recoveryGuard: actual-next-verse departure recovery fraction among eligible origins must be at least the shuffled-next-verse recovery fraction in the same lane; recovery is otherwise descriptive and is not itself a significance test
evaluation.replicationRule: A representation supports verse-boundary continuity only if its primary gate and recovery guard pass in BOTH sealed holdout and control.

secondary.realRecoveryFraction: fraction of eligible unresolved origins whose actual next verse produces F
secondary.meanAndMedianDistance: reported separately for real and shuffled resolved continuations
secondary.realOnlyAndShuffleOnlyCounts: reported to expose asymmetry hidden by the common-resolved primary contrast
